reason: The text explicitly portrays the common people (הָעָם) as active agents with substantial agency throughout the narrative. They initiate the transgression by collectively deciding that Moses has been delayed, gathering before Aaron, and demanding he make gods for them (וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֵלָיו ק֣וּם׀ עֲשֵׂה־ לָ֣נוּ אֱלֹהִ֗ים). The people then actively remove their own gold earrings (וַיִּתְפָּֽרְקוּ כָּל־ הָעָם אֶת־ נִזְמֵי הַזָּהָב), bring the materials to Aaron, worship the calf, make sacrifices, and participate in eating, drinking, and revelry. Aaron himself explicitly acknowledges that the people compelled his action (וַיֹּאמְרוּ לִי עֲשֵׂה־ לָנוּ אֱלֹהִים). Rather than being passive subjects, the non-leader majority demonstrates decisive agency that actually drives the narrative and compels the leader Aaron to respond to their demands.
